anomalies.observed: R60 has pin 2 on ESTOP_OUT and pin 1 on Net-(D30-K2). The second LED of D30 has its anode (A2, pin 4) also on ESTOP_OUT. The LED's anode and its series resistor's far end are therefore on the same net, so the LED has no forward voltage and cannot conduct. R59, the mirror of R60 for the first LED of D30, returns to GND.
anomalies.expected: The series resistor for the second LED of D30 should return to GND, as R59 does for the first LED, so that the LED lights when ESTOP_OUT drives its anode.
anomalies.impact: The ESTOP_OUT status LED (second half of D30) never lights, and the 130R resistor is in a closed loop on ESTOP_OUT, so it draws no useful current. The fault gives no E-stop status indication and may hide a driver fault.

anomalies.observed: R36 is valued 24k, but its library description and MPN specify a 24Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω ±5%').
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the 24Ω part the description and MPN specify, or the MPN and description should be corrected to the 24k part.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R36") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24Ω part was fitted, the VOUTP–VOUTN network would dissipate far more power than the 125mW rating allows; if the 24k value is correct, the sourcing record is wrong and the BOM will be wrong.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only to the anodes of D14 and D23 and to the cathode of D4. No source (regulator, buffer output or switch) drives it, unlike the sibling net /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, which is driven by U34 pin 4.
anomalies.expected: A status-LED supply net of this kind should be driven from a 3.3V (or switched 3.3V) source so the Ethernet and power LEDs can light.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity/link LEDs D14 and D23 and the D4 indicator cannot be powered and will never light, so their status indication is lost. This is only a moderate-confidence finding because the spec does not describe these LEDs.

parsed.summary: The strongest candidate is R60, whose far end is on ESTOP_OUT instead of GND, which shorts out the second D30 LED, unlike its mirror R59. Lower-confidence candidates are a mismatched R36 value and an undriven LED supply net; the rest of the netlist is consistent with the specification.
